provenance.install: docker pull ghcr.io/sec3-product/x-ray:latest, the project's own image
provenance.note: sec3 was formerly Soteria; X-Ray is the open-source successor to their earlier scanner. Quiet since March 2026.

run.reason: The 2026-08-31 invocation was not written into any artefact here. X-Ray compiles Rust to LLVM IR, and B3 established that neither corpus currently compiles: anchor-lang 0.20.1 is yanked so corpus 1 does not resolve, and 7 of the built corpus-2 cases have no src/lib.rs so cargo will not parse them. Re-running it is blocked on the corpus, not on the command.
run.invocation_evidence: What is known: the official container ghcr.io/sec3-product/x-ray:latest, pulled 2026-08-31, over corpus 1 with paths under /tmp/xray_c1. A per-case log exists at raw/xray-c1-raw.json.log; the command that produced it does not.

evidence.reason: a per-case run log exists for corpus 1, but how each run was classified is not recorded, so the classifier cannot be checked against X-Ray's own output the way radar's was

sample.rule_name: The account is missing owner check

positive_control.sample_source: the shape of raw/xray-c1-raw.json, with one finding substituted for the fix site of the synthetic case

measurements.note: 4 / 11 nominal, 2 / 11 real, scored with the CORRECTED mapping. The pre-registered mapping narrowed rule 1019 to one class on the strength of a vendor blog post, and that scored a real detection as zero. Both maps are kept in mappings/xray.json and error 17 is the reason two readings are now registered before every run.
